lines.text: Millions of people open private browsing windows believing their traffic is completely invisible.
In truth, Incognito Mode hides nothing from the internet. It is simply a browser that deletes its own local history file when you close the tab.
The second you type a web address, your operating system fires an unencrypted UDP packet on port fifty-three to resolve the domain name.
Even under modern HTTPS encryption, the TLS handshake broadcasts the Server Name Indication in plain text across your local Wi-Fi and Internet provider.
Commercial tracking networks don't even need cookies: they query your device's graphics card, screen dimensions, and system fonts to generate a unique digital fingerprint.
In twenty twenty-four, Google agreed to destroy billions of browsing records to settle a five-billion-dollar lawsuit over tracking Incognito users.
Incognito Mode protects you from one person: whoever borrows your physical laptop tomorrow. From the internet, you are in plain sight.
